none: Qur’an translation text only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing refers to each person's deeds being weighed and judgment rendered on the Last Day.
rows.anchor: weighing” of every individual’s deeds and the judgment rendered upon them on the Last Day

rows.speaker: Ṭ
rows.claim: The weighing is true because it is just.
rows.anchor: “weighing” is true in that it is just (Ṭ)

rows.speaker: Ṭ
rows.claim: A heavy balance belongs to those with many good deeds or with good deeds outweighing bad ones.
rows.anchor: heavy for those who have accumulated many good deeds or for those whose good deeds outweigh bad ones(Ṭ)

rows.speaker: Ṭ
rows.claim: A light balance belongs to those whose evil deeds outweigh their good deeds.
rows.anchor: light (v. 9) for those whose evil deeds have outweighed good ones

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says nothing is heavier in the balance than good character.
rows.anchor: Nothing is heavier in the balance than good character

rows.speaker: R
rows.claim: Another report indicates that belief in God’s oneness and Muhammad’s prophethood outweighs a vast record of sins.
rows.anchor: belief in the One God and in the prophethood of Muhammad outweighs even a vast record of error and sin (R)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance image is a metaphor for Divine Judgment and appears in other Qur’anic passages.
rows.anchor: image of a balance weighing good and evil deeds is used in other Quranic passages as a metaphor for Divine Judgment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment image accords with Qur’anic commands to weigh fairly and honestly in commercial dealings.
rows.anchor: repeated Quranic injunctions to weigh with justice and integrity in commercial transactions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance also fits the Qur’anic theme that creation is in due balance and that God sets the balance for the created order.
rows.anchor: God creates all things “in due balance” and thus “sets [or sends down] the balance”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together these themes suggest a universal cosmic balance that grounds equitable transactions and measures human acts for recompense in the next life.
rows.anchor: suggests the existence of a universal “balance” that is in the nature of all things in the cosmos

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the questioning in 7:6, weighing does not mean God needs an external source of information or judgment to know how people should be judged.
rows.anchor: should not be understood to mean that God needs a source of information or judgment outside Himself

rows.speaker: Z
rows.claim: The weighing rebukes wrongdoers by making them acknowledge their wrongdoing and abandon excuses.
rows.anchor: serve as a form of rebuke that forces wrongdoers to acknowledge their wrongdoing and surrender all attempts to excuse their actions (Z)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance assures people that they have not been wronged because all deeds are judged by the same scale.
rows.anchor: assure human beings that they have not been wronged, since all deeds are weighed according to the same scale

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community has a fixed term after which it ceases to exist on earth; the term cannot be advanced or delayed.
rows.anchor: a fixed term that can be neither “advanced” nor “delayed” and after which they will cease to exist on earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term for communities is also referenced in several other verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Individual people and humanity as a whole also have an appointed term concerning earthly life.
rows.anchor: Individual human beings and humanity as a whole are also said to have a “fixed” or “appointed” term as far as life in this world is concerned
